cases.summary: The peer runtime (this runner re-run as `fixture --peer`, its own authority, store and machine id ...c3) is added with the real machine.add over an argv transport that runs the binary under test as `ovis-terminal connect`; the hello boot proof answers a fresh challenge. machine.list lists it connected. terminal.run with machine {name: peer} and peer/parent addresses reach only the peer: the peer's parent exits while the local parent of the same name stays live at incarnation 1 with no kills. The peer process is then SIGSTOPped: a call to it ends deadline_exceeded at the 3 s remote deadline while machine.list and a local call answer; after SIGCONT the same line still serves the peer (the server now honours the actor's $/cancelRequest instead of closing the connection).

cases.summary: machine.add with a credential the peer never issued is auth_failed and with another expected machine id is trust_mismatch; neither records a machine. machine.add over SSH (the runtime's fixed `ssh -T -e none -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -- peer.loopback ovis-terminal connect` argument vector, carried by an sshd-free loopback `ssh` on the fixture's search path that accepts only that vector) refuses a foreign credential as auth_failed and a destination that ssh would reinterpret (`-oProxyCommand=id`) as invalid_params before anything is spawned, then adds the peer over the same SSH path. After the peer is added over SSH, an address qualified by an unknown machine is not_found at params.target.address and nothing runs locally, and an observe-only principal's input.send to peer/parent is forbidden before anything is sent to the peer.
